llama.raw_text: Black spots with concentric rings in a bull's eye pattern with a yellow margin. Fruit gets infected through the calyx or stem attachment; black concentric rings on fruits. Irregular leaf spots mostly appear from the marginal portion of leaves. In many tomato cultivars, the symptoms are V-shaped and progress towards the midrib. These lesions are having prominent yellowing on their outer margin due to a host-specific toxin produced by the pathogen. Mostly disease appears in the vegetative phase of the plant growth before flowering. Early blight is first observed on the plants as small, black lesions mostly on the older foliage.

llama.raw_text: Rhizoctonia fruit rot is the most serious disease of kharif tomato. Symptoms appear as rhythmic rotting of fruits coming with the soil contact. Rotting is followed by cracking and fungal growth over it. Lower portion of fruits are usually infected which come into contact with the soil. To prevent the disease, keep the fruits off the soil by staking the plants. Ensure proper drainage in the field.

Young larvae feed on tender foliage. Mature larvae bore circular holes. Thrust only a part of its body into fruit and eat the inner content. Eggs hatch in about 3-4 days and the first instars larvae initially feed on the leaves and migrate to the developing green fruit later. The larvae bore into the fruits with the posterior end outside the hole.

llama.raw_text: Root-knot nematodes cause root galls on the feeder roots and sometimes affect the entire root system showing heavy galling. This affects the uptake of nutrition and water and the plants show wilting during warmer part of the day. This causes stunted plants with yellow foliage resulting in yield reduction. Infected plants in patches in the field. Formation of galls on host root system is the primary symptom. Roots branch profusely starting from the gall tissue causing a 'beard root' symptom. Infected roots become knobby and knotty. In severely infected plants the root system is reduced and the rootlets are almost completely absent. The roots are seriously hampered in their function of uptake and transport of water and nutrients.

Downward rolling and crinkling of the leaves; older leaves become leathery and brittle. Shortened internodes and more side branches give a bushy appearance. The virus is spread by whiteflies (Bemisia tabaci). Leaves show downward rolling, curling, twisting, and chlorosis. Plants show stunting, shortening of internodes, bushy appearance, no flowering, and fruiting later.
